amstar2_items.justification: Research questions and eligibility criteria do not follow a PICO structure; inclusion was based solely on geographic/topical relevance (household sanitation/FSM in Kigali or Rwanda) and publication period (2013–2024, or earlier unamended government documents), without defined interventions/exposures or comparators.
No prospectively registered protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF) or pre-specified written review protocol is reported anywhere in the manuscript, nor are protocol deviations discussed.

Section 2.1 explains why both scientific studies and governmental/regulatory publications were included ("The approach of reviewing both scientific and government publications was chosen to allow a broad understanding of the situation of household FSM in Kigali").

Authors searched two bibliographic databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect) alongside Google Scholar, ResearchGate, Google, and institutional websites and listed five search phrases, but provided no exact search strings/dates, no justification for the 2013–2024 publication date restriction (acknowledged as a potential bias on p. 21) or language limits, and no reference-list checking or expert consultation.

Section 2.1 states that "a total of 270 publications were screened by two reviewers based on the set inclusion and exclusion criteria, and 73 were retained for the review", though independence and conflict-resolution procedures are not detailed.
Duplicate data extraction is not reported in Section 2, and the Author Contributions statement (p. 21) credits "Data collection, original draft writing, M.L.M." to a single author.

No list of excluded full-text publications with per-study reasons for exclusion is provided in the main text, appendices, or listed supplementary materials (Table S1 is only the PRISMA 2020 checklist), and Figure 1 (PRISMA flow diagram) renders as empty boxes without counts or exclusion reasons in the PDF.

Appendix A (Table A1) lists only title, year, broad thematic scope tags, and citation number for the 40 scientific publications, omitting study designs, sample sizes, populations, specific settings, methods, and quantitative outcomes; 10 of the 33 government reports are also absent from summary tables.

Authors appraised 29 empirical studies using an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cross-sectional studies (Table A2, covering sample selection, comparability/confounders, and outcome assessment, though omitting selective outcome reporting), while Table A3 is mislabeled as the JBI Checklist for Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses yet actually applies JBI Text and Opinion items even to included systematic/scoping reviews ([55], [67]), and 33 government documents were only checked for website authenticity.
Sources of funding for the individual included studies are not reported anywhere in the text or appendices.
No meta-analysis or quantitative pooling was performed; synthesis used thematic, narrative, and descriptive methods.

Section 2.3 notes that 3 scientific publications were rated as poor quality (e.g., [44] scored 2/9 and [21] scored 3/9 in Table A3) yet retained because "their findings aligned with high-quality studies", and Results/Discussion tables (Tables 4, 5, 8) synthesize claims and recommendations from poor-quality sources alongside higher-rated studies without weighting or risk-of-bias caveats.

Section 4.4 briefly notes that data across studies were not consistently aligned, preventing direct comparison, without investigating or explaining methodological, settlement-level, or measurement sources of heterogeneity across the included studies.
Pages 21–22 explicitly declare "Funding: This research received no external funding" and "Conflicts of Interest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest."

raw_response.methodological_notes: 1. Scope & Criterion 2/3 fit: Self-described as a PRISMA 2020 'Systematic Review', this paper is functionally a hybrid city-level scoping/thematic and policy synthesis covering both scientific literature and Rwandan legal/regulatory documents on household fecal sludge management (FSM) in Kigali. It strongly satisfies narrow Criterion 2 by analyzing Rwanda's institutional mandates, 23 laws/policies/regulations/standards/guidelines (Section 3.4, Table 7), exhauster licensing and emptying service regulations, tariff/cross-subsidy rules, and landlord–tenant shared-latrine maintenance responsibilities. 2. Internal count discrepancy: Abstract, Section 2.1, and Section 2.3 report 73 included publications (40 scientific publications + 33 government publications), whereas Discussion (Section 4.1) and Conclusions (Section 5) inconsistently state 68 included publications (36 scientific + 32 government). 3. List completeness & primary-study overlap notes: All 40 included scientific publications are completely tabulated in Appendix A (Table A1) and Appendix B (Tables A2–A3) and extracted above (noting that 4 of the 40—[21], [44], [55], [67]—are themselves secondary reviews/syntheses). Of the 33 government publications, 23 regulatory/policy/standard documents are tabulated in Table 7 while the remaining 10 government statistical/sector/audit reports (e.g., NISR EICV4/EICV5/RPHC5/RDHS, MININFRA BLJSR, OAG 2016 audit, RBC 2024 report) are only cited inline; p. 3 states that all included publications are in Supplementary Materials, though p. 21 lists only Table S1 (PRISMA 2020 Checklist). DOIs are not printed in the reference list (only '[CrossRef]' hyperlinks). 4. Appraisal & reporting anomalies: Figure 1 (PRISMA 2020 flow diagram, p. 4) renders as blank boxes without text/counts in the published PDF, and Table A3 (p. 30) is titled 'JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for systematic reviews and research syntheses' but actually uses the 6-item JBI Checklist for Text and Opinion even when scoring included systematic/scoping reviews ([55], [67]).
raw_response.review_design_self_description: systematic review (PRISMA 2020-guided mixed scientific and government policy/regulatory synthesis using thematic, narrative, and descriptive analysis)
